pin_ordering_trace.question: does the top page-directory object already have pinned pages and a DMA address when init_ppgtt_regs reads px_dma
pin_ordering_trace.answer: yes; traced end to end in the pinned drm-kmod tree
chain: gen8_ppgtt_create allocates and initialises the VM, then calls gen8_init_scratch, then gen8_alloc_top_pd (gt/gen8_ppgtt.c:1056-1060)
gen8_alloc_top_pd calls __alloc_pd (kzalloc + kcalloc entries, gt/intel_ppgtt.c:35-51), then vm->alloc_pt_dma to create the backing object, then map_pt_dma on it (gt/gen8_ppgtt.c:933-946)
map_pt_dma pins the object through i915_gem_object_pin_map_unlocked and marks it unshrinkable (gt/intel_gtt.c:115-119); pinning is what establishes the sg DMA addresses that px_dma later reads
only after that does gen8_alloc_top_pd fill the entries with px_dma-derived values (fill_page_dma, gt/gen8_ppgtt.c:948) and mark the page directory pinned (atomic_inc(px_used), :949)
ppgtt->pd is assigned only when gen8_alloc_top_pd returned successfully (gt/gen8_ppgtt.c:1060-1065)
init_ppgtt_regs runs later, when a context is created on that VM (gt/intel_lrc.c:945 via lrc_init_regs), so the read of px_dma(ppgtt->pd) happens strictly after the pin and DMA mapping
failure_rollback: if map_pt_dma fails, gen8_alloc_top_pd goes to err_pd and calls free_pd, which is free_px(vm, px_pt(px), 1): it frees the entry array, does i915_gem_object_put on the backing object exactly once, and frees the directory (gt/intel_ppgtt.c:71-85)

gen8_ppgtt_create then takes err_put and calls i915_vm_put (gt/gen8_ppgtt.c:1082-1084); gen8_ppgtt_cleanup guards its teardown with if (ppgtt->pd) (gt/gen8_ppgtt.c:232), and ppgtt->pd is still NULL on that path, so the already-freed directory cannot be freed twice

port_primitives_at_these_sites.mutex: sx_xlock on XNU, non-recursive, may sleep; every mutex site in this path is thread context and compatible
port_primitives_at_these_sites.spinlock_irqsave: spinlock_t is a sleeping MTX_DEF mutex and spin_lock_irqsave only zeroes the flags, so interrupt masking, preemption disable and the SPL are all absent; only the port's own MTX_SPIN locks used by RCU and tasklet state actually mask interrupts
port_primitives_at_these_sites.queue_work: taskqueue_enqueue plus a sleeping mutex, so it may sleep; every site here is thread context, including the ones reached from the RCU callback, which runs on the port's RCU task thread
port_primitives_at_these_sites.kfree_rcu: call_rcu with the offset encoded; the free happens later on a plain kernel thread with no XNU lock held, so it does not free from a lock-holding context
port_primitives_at_these_sites.rcu_barrier: drains one shared RCU task, so a blocking callback stalls every grace period
port_primitives_at_these_sites.workqueue_drain: drain_workqueue sets wq->draining, after which queue_work silently drops work and flush_work returns immediately for an unqueued work
